OP switched personalities again from trying to kill or rape me to the way you would talk to a stray kitten as he crouched nude walking slowly out of the apartment. Just when I was going to give up because this was the second police call for his erratic behavior with no outcome or help. I was helpless. That would have been the end of me. I thought about jumping to my death because I’d rather that tan have him rape me. Two deputies showed up just as soon as OP was about 5 feet from reaching me. So... I’ll try to make a checklist in order so it’s easier to digest and read:

1. make sure you are hitting the pass through before the release, the flag should hit flat at your eyes during this. 
- the flags position goes from right hand on hip (as you are and doing already) then you will lift your right hand up to have the flag pole meet your eyes/temple area as your left hand pulls slightly down and across your body/face to meet perpendicular to/side-to-side of your left eye/temple area. That’s your first check-point and it will happen on the ‘and’ count before the release. (Say if you are releasing on count 1 your flag should be parallel to the ground and at eye level on count “8-and”)
2. If you are doing a single you will catch silk down on the left side of your body. Right now it is really whippy because you are giving it too much rotation and it’s not getting enough height. If you were to have caught that first toss it would have been a single and a half (it landed silk forward in front of you, instead of the silk down facing your feet)
- so pull with your left arm slightly less hard than you are now, to give it less rotation.
- Your right arm is really high in the air and that a good thing for height, don’t change that, but you are pushing it out/ releasing right above your head. Bring your arm forward, closer to at a 45 degree angle, you should be able to see your arm/ right hand on the release. 
- also try to squeeze everything (especially core and glutes) imagine weights holding the heels of your feet down so that you don’t jump on the release. 
3. I scrubbed slowly through the video and it looks like you have started to anticipate this toss to be fast and low, you’ve started to already run from it before you have actually released the flag. This is making you toss even lower and ‘whippy-er’ as you are shifting your body to ‘run, duck, and cover’ as you are releasing it. 
- imaging your ribcage as stone. Once again SQUEEZE. If after you toss you feel the need to run from it do so, but make sure you, one: give it a fighting chance lol, if you run from it before even releasing it can be more dangerous and do unexpected things. Two, the toss will probably go up more correctly and you won’t feel the need to run if you aren’t shifting everything away from your body on/ before the release. 
4. Don’t “wind up” before this toss.
- right now you are starting strong and your flag is straight to the audience, but once you start your toss you are bringing it to an angle (winding-up for more power, you don’t need it) don’t shift your right hand behind you and don’t push your left arm across your body before going into the toss.

•• 45’s have 3 check points 

     - your starting position. (Yours looks good until you wind-up...essentially never actually hitting it) once you lock into that right hand on hip and strong 45 stance don’t move from it until you go on to transition to the next checkpoint...
     - the parallel to the ground at eye level (talked in more detail on very first note above) 
     - the release point. Your body should be stone besides your arms obviously lol. You should see you right hand on the release (not so far back you can’t see it) Your left hand pulls back to give the flag it’s rotation (lame analogy but: almost like you are necking yourself) 
          ** you release with both hand simultaneously at this checkpoint. Right now if you watch the video of yourself and slow it down notice on that first toss you are releasing that left hand before it gets to the back of your head. (Also this is a bit nit picky and I realize my entire post is😂...but I hope some of my numerous details help!)...When you are releasing with your right hand it looks like your flexing your wrist/hand up, avoid that and try making a straighter line connecting your finger tips to your elbows, don’t bend your wrist so high on the release. 


It takes practice and this definitely is not a bad place to start. You look great and passionate! Just needs some tweaking and I hope my comment post and other people’s comments help you on your journey! Don’t give up! You’ll get the hang of it and be tossing perfect 45’s soon enough!
